title: Assistant Accountant
description:
NXTGEN is working with an established, business to recruit an Assistant Accountant for its finance team. This Assistant Accountant position offers the opportunity to develop your month-end experience within a team where people have progressed.

As Assistant Accountant, you'll work closely with the Management Accountants to prepare monthly management accounts and manufacturer reporting. You'll also work with department managers to investigate discrepancies, answer queries and help them understand the financial performance of their site.

The role combines hands-on accounting with analysis and process improvement, giving you exposure to how finance supports the day-to-day running of a motor retail business.

Key responsibilities as Assistant Accountant
- Support the preparation of monthly management accounts, including accruals and prepayments
- Prepare balance sheet reconciliations, investigate differences and follow up outstanding items
- Assist with monthly manufacturer reporting and process weekly manufacturer bonuses
- Authorise daily payments in line with company procedures
- Monitor outstanding and ageing debt, following up and reporting on overdue balances
- Support vehicle and parts stocktakes, investigate variances and report findings to management
- Respond to management accounts queries and highlight discrepancies or control concerns
- Work with the Management Accountants to identify improvements to financial processes and reporting
- Maintain accurate financial records and supporting documentation

What we're looking for

You'll have experience within a busy accounts department and be keen to build on your accounting knowledge. AAT Level 3 or an equivalent qualification is preferred, although candidates qualified by experience will also be considered.

Strong numerical skills, attention to detail and confidence using Microsoft packages are essential. You'll be comfortable investigating discrepancies, communicating with colleagues across the business and following queries through to resolution.

Knowledge of Pinnacle DMS would be useful, but isnt essential.

This Assistant Accountant role is based on site in Norwich and would suit someone looking to broaden their experience in management accounts while contributing to an expanding business.

To find out more about this Assistant Accountant opportunity, contact Grace at NXTGEN Recruitment.

title: Remote Conveyancing Paralegal
company: LEGAL TALENT PARTNERS LIMITED - Agency - Permanent
description:
Remote Conveyancing Paralegal

£30,000-40,000

Quality. Technology. Flexibility. A Better Way to Do Conveyancing.

We're partnering with a fast-growing, forward-thinking residential conveyancing firm that is using technology, smarter processes and a collaborative team structure to change the way property law is delivered.

The firm is built around a simple idea: conveyancing should be simpler, clearer and faster - for clients and the people delivering it.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for greater autonomy, better technology, a sustainable workload and the flexibility of a fully remote role, this could be an excellent next move.

Why This Role Stands Out

This is not a traditional conveyancing environment where paralegals are left to manage overwhelming caseloads with little support.

You'll work within small, collaborative teams, with regular check-ins, structured 1-to-1s, feedback and personalised training.

The firm takes a quality over quantity approach to workload, maintaining sustainable caseloads and giving teams capacity to deal with peaks without compromising client service.

You'll benefit from:
- Sustainable caseloads and a strong focus on work-life balance
- Small, collaborative teams
- Regular support, feedback and development
- Bespoke technology designed around legal teams
- A culture where asking for help is encouraged
- The opportunity to influence how technology and processes develop
- Fully remote working with genuine flexibility

The result? A more manageable workload, better support and the freedom to focus on delivering excellent conveyancing rather than simply processing as many files as possible.

The Role

As a Conveyancing Paralegal, you'll be an integral part of a residential conveyancing team, working alongside lawyers and other paralegals to deliver an excellent client service.

You'll work across freehold and leasehold sales, purchases and remortgages, taking ownership of your matters while working collaboratively with the wider team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Progressing residential sales, purchases and remortgages
- Handling freehold sales with minimal supervision
- Managing most leasehold sale enquiries with minimal supervision
- Managing most freehold purchase enquiries with minimal supervision
- Liaising with clients, solicitors, estate agents and other third parties
- Proactively identifying issues and keeping transactions moving
- Reviewing and responding to enquiries
- Maintaining clear, jargon-free communication
- Using the firm's technology to manage your caseload efficiently
- Identifying and resolving potential issues before they become blockers
- Providing feedback to improve systems and processes

The firm's technology has been developed specifically around its conveyancing process, and legal professionals are encouraged to provide feedback on the tools they use every day.

About you

You'll ideally have:
- Strong experience in residential conveyancing
- Experience handling freehold sales with limited supervision
- Experience dealing with leasehold sale enquiries
- Experience dealing with freehold purchase enquiries
- Confidence communicating with clients and third parties
- A proactive approach to progressing transactions
- Strong organisation and attention to detail
- Excellent communication and problem-solving skills
- Confidence working independently in a remote environment
- An interest in using technology to improve legal work

You don't need to be qualified. This role is suited to an experienced paralegal with strong technical conveyancing skills who is ready to take greater ownership of their work.

Although fully remote, you won't be left alone with a laptop and a pile of files. Regular team check-ins, 1-to-1s and ongoing feedback are built into the firm's approach.

The Culture:

This is a firm deliberately doing things differently.

Rather than chasing maximum utilisation, it takes a sustainable approach to workload, helping teams maintain consistent service levels while giving people room to deal with the unexpected.

Its technology helps allocate work, streamline processes and keep teams informed, while its remote-working model is built around communication, supervision, feedback and development.

There's also a strong culture of transparency and continuous improvement. People are encouraged to share ideas, challenge processes and help shape the future of the business.

The Package
- £30,000-£40,000 depending on experience
- Fully remote - work from anywhere in the UK
- Flexible working hours
- 25 days' holiday + 3 days at Christmas + Bank Holidays
- Full home-working setup and equipment provided
- Comprehensive private healthcare
- Free access to Spill mental health and wellbeing support
- Company pension scheme
- Enhanced maternity, paternity and adoption leave
- Growth Shares, giving employees an opportunity to share in the long-term success of the business
- Fully paid-for annual company weekend
- Structured development and genuine progression opportunities

The firm's flexible approach is a key part of its culture, with many employees working flexible hours or part-time. The focus is on creating working patterns that work for both the individual and the wider team.

If you're an experienced conveyancing paralegal looking for a genuinely modern, supportive and flexible place to build your career, we'd love to hear from you.

title: HR Administrator
company: Macildowie Recruitment and Retention - Agency - Permanent
description:
HR and Compliance Administrator

Temporary - Initial 4-6 weeks
Marham
Full-time, ideally 5 days per week
Immediate start

Macildowie are delighted to be supporting a not-for-profit organisation in Marham with the appointment of a HR & Compliance Administrator on a temporary basis.

This is an important short-term assignment supporting the organisation with a detailed review of its staff records and wider compliance documentation. The role would suit someone who is highly organised, methodical and confident working through large volumes of administrative information, rather than someone looking for a traditional HR role.

Working closely with the existing team, you will help ensure that staff files are complete, accurate and fully up to date, while also supporting a range of wider administrative tasks across the setting.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Auditing staff files to ensure they are complete, accurate and compliant.
- Chasing outstanding DBS identification documentation and ensuring records are correctly maintained.
- Reviewing staff qualifications to confirm they are current, relevant and supported by the appropriate evidence.
- Checking staff suitability declarations are completed and up to date.
- Ensuring appropriate documentation is in place where required, including risk assessments, healthcare plans and occupational health recommendations.
- Tracking outstanding actions through to completion and maintaining accurate compliance records.
- Completing and updating rotas and other staff administration.
- Supporting the completion and maintenance of allergy plans.
- Working through the wider compliance action plan and helping to close outstanding actions.
- Identifying gaps in documentation and helping to put effective administrative processes in place to prevent these recurring.

About you

We are looking for someone who is organised, thorough and comfortable working independently through detailed administrative tasks. You will need excellent attention to detail and the ability to identify missing information, follow up with colleagues and maintain accurate records.

Previous HR or compliance experience would be useful, particularly within an education, care, charity or other regulated environment, but this is fundamentally an administrative role and we would consider candidates with strong general administration experience who can demonstrate a methodical approach.

You will need to be comfortable handling confidential information and working through paper-based records, with the ability to prioritise and manage a varied workload.

A current DBS certificate with the individual registered on the DBS Update Service is essential for this assignment.

The role

This is an initial four-to-six-week temporary assignment, with the potential to extend depending on the workload and progress made.

The role is fully site-based in Marham, as the majority of the work involves reviewing and updating physical staff files held at the setting. Unfortunately, there is no scope for the role to be carried out remotely.

Ideally, the organisation is looking for someone who can work five days per week, as the additional resource will enable this important compliance work to be completed as quickly as possible. Four days per week may be considered for the right person if necessary.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced administrator to make an immediate and tangible contribution, helping the organisation ensure its records and compliance processes are fully up to date and inspection-ready.

The role involves coordinating interviews, maintaining candidate records, processing compliance documentation, and delivering excellent service to candidates, clients, and hiring managers.

Key ResponsibilitiesRecruitment Administration
- Support the end-to-end recruitment process for temporary, permanent, and contract vacancies.
- Create and post job advertisements across multiple job boards and social media platforms.
- Screen applications and accurately update candidate records within the recruitment database.
- Arrange interviews and assessment centres, coordinating schedules for candidates and hiring managers.
- Prepare interview packs and recruitment documentation.

Candidate Management
- Act as the first point of contact for candidates throughout the recruitment process.
- Obtain and process right-to-work documentation and pre-employment checks.
- Chase outstanding compliance documents and references.
- Ensure candidates are kept informed of application progress in a professional and timely manner.

Compliance & Onboarding
- Complete recruitment compliance checks, including referencing, DBS checks, qualifications, and eligibility to work verification.
- Ensure all recruitment activities comply with employment legislation, GDPR, and company policies.
- Prepare onboarding documentation and support new starters throughout the onboarding process.
- Maintain accurate audit trails and electronic records.

Administrative Support
- Manage recruitment inboxes and telephone enquiries.
- Prepare offer letters, contracts, and candidate information packs.
- Produce reports and recruitment statistics when required.
- Maintain accurate records on recruitment systems and databases.

Essential Skills & Experience
- Previous administration experience.
- Excellent organisational and time management skills.
- Strong attention to detail and accuracy.
- Ability to prioritise workloads and work to deadlines.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, including Outlook, Word, Excel, and Teams.
- Experience managing confidential information appropriately.
- Strong customer service skills.

Desirable Skills & Experience
- Previous recruitment or HR administration experience.
- Knowledge of compliance processes and employment legislation.

Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. When necessary, enter requests for home visits onto the computer, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to Duty Doctor. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non NHS) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Monitor and complete clinical system tasks as required by the Reception Supervisor, Practice Manager and GPs. Premises: Open up premises at the start of the day when first to arrive, de-activate alarm and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. When last to leave at the end of the day, ensure that the building is totally secured, internal lights are off and the alarm activated. Undertake any other additional duties appropriate to the post as requested by the Reception Supervisor or the Practice Manager. Attend team and practice meetings. Give results and/or information to the patient as directed by the doctors. Accept and ensure all specimens are clearly labelled and pass on to Healthcare staff for appropriate recording prior to collection by hospital transport. Confidentiality: In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines. Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks. Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills. Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards. Reporting potential risks identified to the Health and Safety Team immediately. Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation. Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues. Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Attending all training courses and sessions deemed as mandatory by the Practice Manager. Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk. Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision. Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance. Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs. Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. Communication: The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members. Communicate effectively with patients and carers. Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply practice policies, standards and guidance. Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work. Participate in audit where appropriate.

The role is to provide a full reception service to outpatient clinics ensuring all patient information, referrals and appointments are appropriately processed within Trust guidelines. The candidate will offer the highest standard of customer care to patients, visitors and other service users, adhering to Departmental guidelines, Standard Operating Procedures and the Trust's Code of Values and Behaviours. As a Receptionist you will provide the first point of contact for patients, relatives and carers arriving for an outpatient appointment, presenting a professional, calm and confident manner in line with the Trust's Values and Behaviours. You will provide a full reception service to the outpatient clinic including, but not limited to: - Maintaining accurate information and patient demographics within Trust PAS system.- Supporting clinical staff in ensuring the Trust meets accessible information standards for patients with communication difficulties.- Ensuring patients' arrival and departure times are electronically captured.- Distribution, collation and inputting of clinic outcomes.- Book future appointments and recording of non-attendances. Please see the Job Description and Person Specification for a full and comprehensive overview for this position.

title: Senior Administrator
description: This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced Senior Administrator to join a dynamic and forward-looking Primary Care Network (PCN), based in Thetford, Norfolk. We are seeking an enthusiastic, hard-working, and caring person to support the continued growth and development of Breckland Alliance PCN. The role is interesting and varied, and provides an excellent career development opportunity. Undertaking a variety of administrative and compliance duties including the provision of secretarial and clerical support to our Primary Care Network (PCN) team including Clinical Director and PCN Business Manager Supporting the PCN Business Manager to maintain policy and procedure documents and risk registers Assisting with the review of compliance standards across the PCN Demonstrating a positive attitude towards digital transformation, with a willingness to learn and utilise emerging technologies, including Microsoft Copilot and AI agents Seeking opportunities to improve efficiency, automate routine tasks, enhance productivity and support modern ways of working Organisation of meetings including agenda formation, minutes and accurate record keeping Producing external communications, including via social media, in respect of PCN activities Administration support of PCN services such as, but not limited to, Vasectomy service and Travel Vaccines Maintaining high standards of communication across the PC Arranging training courses for the PCN, including booking and communicating invitations appropriately Monitoring email inboxes daily, disseminating information across the PCN Assist with HR and recruitment across the Breckland Alliance (advertising, interview set-up, references, inductions, appraisals, etc.) Assisting with shared staff annual leave and other absence Undertaking any other additional duties reasonable to the role, as requested by the PCN Manager and/or PCN Clinical Director 1.Confidentiality In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, PCN and practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the PCN as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the PCN may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. 2.Health and Safety The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified 3.Equality and Diversity The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognizes the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with practice procedures and policies, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to and of the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights 4.Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the PCN as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work. Attend annual mandatory up-dates on Fire Safety, Resuscitation and Safe Lifting. 5.Quality: The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the PCN, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources. 6. Communication: The post-holder should recognize the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly. 7. Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply PCN policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate
